Docs·Make it lighter

Auto cleanup and Tidy geometry

Small one-click repairs: remove empty parts and empty groups, fix shading, recentre the model and make moves permanent.

Two cards in the right sidebar, under Clean up, hold one-click commands. Each is one undo step.

Auto cleanup

Remove empty parts
Deletes parts that contain no triangles. Files often carry a few of these.
Fix degenerate parts
Removes parts whose triangles have no area, which can confuse the programs that draw them.
Delete empty groups
Removes groups that have no parts left in them.
Deduplicate geometry
Looks for parts whose mesh data is identical to another part’s. See the note below before you use it.

Each command reports what it did, or says that it found nothing.

Be careful with Deduplicate geometry on an assembly. It removes the repeats of a part wherever they stand and keeps the first one, so a set of identical bolts is reduced to a single bolt. Check the parts count afterwards, and press CtrlZ if it took parts you wanted. To remove only copies that sit in the same place, use Stacked copies instead.

Smart optimise starts every run with the first three commands, empty parts, degenerate parts and empty groups, under the name Remove empty and broken parts. It does not run Deduplicate geometry or any of the Tidy geometry commands.

Tidy geometry

Recompute smooth normals
Works out the shading directions of every surface again. Use it when parts look oddly faceted or dark after large changes.
Recentre on origin
Moves the model so the centre of its bounding box sits at 0,0,0.
Bake gizmo transforms
Makes the moves, turns and scalings you did with the gizmo permanent in the mesh itself.
Centre pivot
Moves the pivot of each selected part to the centre of its bounding box. The part does not move on screen.

Flags

The card Filters & flags, under Inspect, marks suspicious parts without changing them:

Flag low-triangle parts
Marks parts with fewer triangles than the slider says.
Flag thin slivers
Marks parts that are extremely long for their width, such as gaskets, wires and decals.

The status bar shows how many parts are flagged. Click that number to isolate them, look at them, and decide what to do.
